Definition: properly, to hammer out (an edge), i.e. to sharpen
BiblicalUsage: lâṭash means to sharpen, and once is enough to see what it is doing. In 1 Samuel 13:20, "to sharpen every man his share"; and in Genesis 4:22, "an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron: and the sister of Tubal-cain [was] Naamah.". In Psalms 7:12, "he will whet his sword".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe sharpening is honest work with a sharp edge — the same skill that keeps a ploughshare cutting can whet a sword, and God notices which one I choose.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
